finding.claim: reconstructJob() falls back to building a Job from unsigned, attacker-writable JSON fields (command/arguments) when the HMAC check is absent or fails, so an unsigned queue file yields an arbitrary callable that Job::exec() invokes via call_user_func_array. This defeats the GHSA-vj3m-2g9h-vm4p HMAC fix for the job queue.
finding.source: Any JSON file placed in the scheduler queue directory (user-data://scheduler/queue/pending/*.json). Precondition: write access to that directory (e.g. from any arbitrary-file-write primitive or a misconfigured web-reachable user-data path).
finding.sink: Job::exec() calling call_user_func_array($this->command, $this->args) (Job.php:542), with command and args taken from the queue item.

trace.note: popNext / pop path: items read from pending/ are passed to reconstructJob()
second call site, same reconstructJob() fallback
HMAC check only runs when both serialized_job and serialized_job_hmac are present
if HMAC missing or mismatched, the serialized path is skipped entirely
if isset($item['command']) — attacker-chosen command string accepted, no allowlist
new Job($item['command'], $args, $item['job_id']) with $args = $item['arguments'] unvalidated
constructor accepts any command/args, no validation
call_user_func_array executes the callable with attacker args (e.g. command='system', arguments=['id'])
moveQueueItem builds paths from item['id'] (from JSON) without sanitising; a crafted id can also rename files outside the queue dir (secondary, same precondition)

finding.guards_checked: HMAC-SHA256 over serialized_job using Security::getNonceKey() (JobQueue.php:474-475) — applies only when HMAC fields are present; allowed_classes restriction (JobQueue.php:480) — only on the signed path; the comment at 489-492 explicitly states the fallback runs 'without trusting their serialized state', but it still trusts command/arguments. No command allowlist, no check that command is a Job-owned closure or method string. Not guarded: the id used in moveQueueItem/writeQueueItem path concatenation.

finding.claim: Per-page index store payloads (pages, children, sorts, taxonomy rows) are unserialized without allowed_classes and without any HMAC, unlike the session, job queue and file cache stores, so a tampered cache DB can instantiate arbitrary classes (PHP object injection).
finding.source: Contents of the SQLite pages index DB under cache://compiled/pages. Precondition: write access to the cache directory; feature is opt-in (system.pages.lazy_index).
finding.sink: unserialize() of DB payload with no allowed_classes restriction.

trace.note: readSerializedRow() selects payload by path from attacker-writable table
@unserialize($payload) — no allowed_classes option, error suppressed, no HMAC
readTaxonomyValue unserializes taxonomy payloads the same way
readTaxonomy unserializes all taxonomy payloads the same way
hydrateIndexedPages: @unserialize($payloads[$path]) — instanceof PageInterface check happens only after unserialize has already run
loadIndexedPage: same pattern, instanceof check after unserialize

finding.guards_checked: The instanceof/is_array checks run after unserialize, so they do not prevent object instantiation or __wakeup/__destruct gadgets. No HMAC over stored payloads (contrast Session.php:108-137, FileCache.php:100-119, JobQueue.php:474). Store is only read when system.pages.lazy_index is enabled. Write precondition is not verified as remotely reachable.

finding.claim: The POST 'blueprint' value is only HTML-escaped and tag-stripped before being used as a blueprint name, so path separators and '..' survive and can select a .yaml file outside blueprints://pages, which is parsed as a blueprint.
finding.source: $_POST['blueprint'] on a page save/edit request. Precondition: an authenticated user with page-edit permission (admin.pages or equivalent).
finding.sink: Blueprint file resolution: 'blueprints://pages/' . $name . '.yaml' passed to the locator and read/parsed as YAML.

trace.note: raw $_POST['blueprint'] read
htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(...)) — does not remove '/' or '..'
$pages->blueprints($this->blueprintName())
blueprints->get($type); on RuntimeException falls back to 'default' only
loadFile($type) with unvalidated name; instances cached by name
$path = $context . $path where context = 'blueprints://pages/' and path = attacker name
'.yaml' appended if missing; no realpath/containment check

finding.guards_checked: strip_tags + htmlspecialchars (Page.php:1503) — no path validation. Contrast FileReader.php:131-150, which does realpath() containment against locator roots; no equivalent here. Impact is read/parse of an arbitrary .yaml file as a blueprint (info disclosure of field definitions/defaults, possible validation/filter bypass for that save), gated by page-edit authorization. Locator handling of '..' segments not verified — treat as PLAUSIBLE until confirmed.
